title: Geometric regularity criterion for smoothness over a field
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum] locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Then $f$ is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] if and only if, for every finitely generated field extension $L/k$ [def-pc-field-extension] and every point $x\in X_L=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}L$ [def-pc-fibre-product], the local ring $\mathcal O_{X_L,x}$ is a regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Here finitely generated means that $L$ is generated as a field over $k$ by finitely many elements; no perfectness, dimension, reducedness, connectedness or separatedness hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 038X (lemma-geometrically-regular-smooth), pointwise equivalence at every point; Tag 038T (definition-geometrically-regular), finitely generated field extensions

proof.text: Assume $f$ smooth and fix a finitely generated field extension $L/k$ and $z\in X_L$. By the affine-local characterization of smoothness in [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], choose a smooth affine neighbourhood $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of the image of $z$, so $k\to A$ is smooth by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-iff-smooth-affine]. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-chart-base-change-iso], the inverse image $U_L$ is the affine open $\operatorname{Spec}(L\otimes_k A)$ of $X_L$, containing $z$. The map $L\to L\otimes_k A$ is smooth by clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-base-change-composition]. Thus its localization at the prime corresponding to $z$ is regular local by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-over-field-regular-local]. It is $\mathcal O_{X_L,z}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization]. This proves the forward implication (indeed for every field extension).

source.place: Tag 038X (lemma-geometrically-regular-smooth), forward implication; algebra.tex Tags 00T4 and 00TT; schemes.tex Tags 01JR and 01HV

proof.text: Conversely assume the regular-local-ring condition. Fix $x\in X$. The definition of locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] provides an affine neighbourhood $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $x$ with $A$ a finite type $k$-algebra. Let $\mathfrak p$ be its prime corresponding to $x$, and put $K=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$. The induced residue field of the zero prime of $k$ is $k$ itself. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-residue-field-extension-finitely-generated] to $k\to A$ proves that $K/k$ is finitely generated as a field, so the assumed condition may be applied with $L=K$.

source.place: Tag 038X (lemma-geometrically-regular-smooth), converse: affine reduction and finitely generated residue field

proof.text: Put $B=K\otimes_k A$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-chart-base-change-iso], $U_K$ is the affine open $\operatorname{Spec}B$ in $X_K$ and its projection to $U$ is induced by $j:A\to B$, $a\mapsto1\otimes a$. The compatible maps $K\to K$ (identity) and $A\to K$ (residue map $\bar a$) yield by [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property] a $K$-algebra map $\epsilon:B\to K$, $\lambda\otimes a\mapsto\lambda\bar a$. This map is surjective since $\epsilon(\lambda\otimes1)=\lambda$. Consequently $\mathfrak q=\ker\epsilon$ is maximal and contracts under $j$ to $\mathfrak p$. Moreover $B/\mathfrak q\cong K$ as $K$-algebras, and $\epsilon$ extends to $B_{\mathfrak q}\to K$ by $b/s\mapsto\epsilon(b)/\epsilon(s)$: the denominator is nonzero exactly when $s\notin\mathfrak q$. Its kernel is $\mathfrak qB_{\mathfrak q}$, so $\kappa(\mathfrak q)\cong K$ as $K$-extensions, by [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime].

The point $z\in U_K\subset X_K$ corresponding to $\mathfrak q$ has regular local ring by the hypothesis and Step 2. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization], this local ring is $B_{\mathfrak q}$. The algebra $B$ is finite type over $K$: if $a_1,\dots,a_n$ generate $A$ over $k$, then $1\otimes a_1,\dots,1\otimes a_n$ generate $B$ over $K$. Its residue extension $\kappa(\mathfrak q)/K$ is the identity extension by Step 3 and is separable by [def-weil-pbc-separable-field-extension]: its only intermediate field is $K$, the transcendence basis is empty, and the minimal polynomials are linear with derivative $1$. The regular-to-smooth implication of [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-separable-residue-smooth], with base field $K$, algebra $B$ and prime $\mathfrak q$, therefore proves $K\to B$ smooth at $\mathfrak q$.

source.place: Tag 00TV (lemma-separable-smooth); agent application at the residue-field rational point

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-at-prime-field-extension-descent] with the field extension $K/k$, finite type algebra $A$, and prime $\mathfrak q\subset K\otimes_k A$. Its contracted prime is $\mathfrak p$ by Step 3 and the required smoothness at $\mathfrak q$ was proved in Step 4. Thus $k\to A$ is smooth at $\mathfrak p$: there is $g\in A\setminus\mathfrak p$ for which $A_g$ is a smooth $k$-algebra.

By [lem-weil-pbc-principal-localization-open-immersion], the localization map identifies $\operatorname{Spec}A_g$ with the open subscheme $D(g)\subset U$. This open contains $x$ because $g\notin\mathfrak p$ and its morphism to $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is smooth by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-iff-smooth-affine]. As $x$ was arbitrary, these neighbourhoods cover $X$. Hence $f$ is smooth by the affine-local characterization stated in [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. The argument is pointwise; for empty $X$ the cover is empty and both conditions are vacuous.
